newsitem.title: UK: Metals Outlook - LME Copper, aluminium eye upside.
newsitem.headline: Metals Outlook - LME Copper, aluminium eye upside.

text.p: Copper's surge to pre-Sumitomo price levels last week should signal further gains in the near term, although a technical correction is likely first, analysts said.
Expectations that Chinese demand is poised to enter the market, combined with tightness emerging in April dates, are also helping maintain the market's bullish tone.

"The uptrend has enjoyed a sudden acceleration and the earlier highs have been cleared, giving good excuse for the move to go even higher yet," said technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge.
Gifford pegged $2,400-$2,450 per tonne as the upcoming targets for three months delivery copper, following its surge above stiff $2,313 resistance last Wednesday.
Copper prices, which have been trending higher since the end of January, finished Friday's afternoon kerb at $2,366, a gain of nearly $40 from Thursday.

The close was near the day's highs, although the metal was unable to convincingly breach stiff resistance at $2,375, which dates back to June 4, 1996. That level would provide the first upside hurdle.
Traders will be keeping their eyes open for signs of Chinese buying, which is widely expected to underpin the market in coming months.
But as a short term concern, some 20,000 tonnes of Chinese copper is currently reported to be in Singapore and some traders fear it could be delivered into LME warehouses.
However, Friday's small increase in LME stocks of 1,875 tonnes, was ignored by the market.
"The feeling in the market is that the recent high backwardation had been responsible for the increases in LME stocks," said analyst Martin Squires of brokers Rudolf Wolff.
"If we see more decreases or small increases like on Friday, I think the market is going to shrug them off."
Aluminium was also poised to spurt higher following a positive close of $1,631 on Friday, which was attained after breaching stiff resistance at $1,615.
Aluminium was expected to target $1,651, and then $1,700, Squires said.
